title: The integral proper projection formula
statement:
Work in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes and their $k$-morphisms. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside an algebraic closure, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$. Use its condensed coefficient ring and its pullbacks $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], the ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], bounded constructible complexes $\Dbc$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and localizing closures with ambient small direct sums [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. All tensor products are the relative derived tensors of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], without completion. The projection formula map is the canonical adjoint transpose of the pullback tensor comparison followed by the tensor of the counit $p^*Rp_*K\to K$ with $p^*L$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact].

1. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the projection formula map
$$Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,Y}}L\longrightarrow Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}p^*L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.
2. For every standing scheme $T$, $\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$ is closed under $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$. The same projection formula map is an isomorphism for $K\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ and $L\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text: For every standing scheme $T$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] applies to its separated finite-type structure map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and makes $T$ qcqs. The integral case of [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2) then gives $\Dctf(T,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ and equality of their localizing closures. Put $\mathcal L_T=\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$. By [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1),(2), the ambient module-object derived category has small direct sums, and $\mathcal L_T$ is the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory containing $\Dbc$ and closed under those sums. Its sums are the ambient sums: fullness restricts the ambient coproduct universal property to test objects in $\mathcal L_T$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), ambient localizing categories and the integral equality Dctf=Dbc made explicit

proof.text: Clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral] asserts that the proper projection formula map is an isomorphism for exactly $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Its hypotheses are met: $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $p$ is proper, and $X,Y$ are standing schemes. This proves (1) by reuse of the existing bounded integral theorem. It is the same uncompleted tensor and the same canonical map; no discrete constant $\mathcal O_E$-coefficient category or étale-origin witness is substituted. The finite-reduction/derived-Nakayama argument of paragraph (1) is already the content of that existing node, rather than a new restatement created here.

source.place: Paragraph (1), bounded integral formula; reuse the existing integral proper theorem, clause (3)

proof.text:
Tensoring in the ambient unbounded category is exact and preserves small direct sums in either variable. Here are the elementary calculations. Fix a K-flat representative $P$ in [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a complex map $a$, the differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Cone}(a)\otimes P)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(a\otimes P))$ by distributing over the two cone summands; it gives the signed shift identification as well. K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex] makes this preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and the cone description of distinguished triangles [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] proves exactness after localization. For sums, the internal-Hom adjunction in [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] gives, naturally in $Z$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\bigoplus_i A_i,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\bigoplus_iA_i,\operatorname{RHom}(C,Z))\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}A_i,Z).$$
This is precisely the universal property of the coproduct with its canonical inclusions, so tensor preserves sums. Symmetry gives the other variable. The sums exist by step 1. These arguments apply to the relative module-object tensor specified in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph (2), exactness and sum preservation of tensor, expanded by its K-flat definition and right adjoint

proof.text: Fix $B\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ and let $\mathcal C_B$ be the full subcategory of the ambient derived category of objects $A$ such that $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\in\mathcal L_T$. Step 3 and the closure properties in step 1 show that $\mathcal C_B$ is replete, triangulated and closed under small sums. The tensor clause of [sk-lem-int-tensor] says that it contains $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. Minimality in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2) gives $\mathcal L_T\subseteq\mathcal C_B$. Thus $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\in\mathcal L_T$ for $A\in\mathcal L_T$ and bounded constructible $B$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), tensor closure: first localizing variable

proof.text: Now fix $A\in\mathcal L_T$ and take the full ambient subcategory $\mathcal E_A$ on objects $B$ with $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\in\mathcal L_T$. Steps 1 and 3 again give repleteness, shifts, triangles and small-sum closure. Step 4 puts $\Dbc$ in $\mathcal E_A$. The same minimality [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](2) gives $\mathcal L_T\subseteq\mathcal E_A$. This proves the tensor-closure assertion of (2) for every standing $T$, with ordinary ambient sums and uncompleted tensor.

source.place: Paragraph (2), tensor closure: second localizing variable

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] with $g=p$, $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, and [det-proper-image-localizing-proper] to $p$. The latter explicitly states that both its required hypotheses hold for integral coefficients in the standing setting; it is not being applied merely conditionally. Step 1 identifies its $\Dctf$ closures with our $\mathcal L_T$. Hence $p^*:\mathcal L_Y\to\mathcal L_X$ and $Rp_*:\mathcal L_X\to\mathcal L_Y$ are exact and preserve small sums. For $K\in\mathcal L_X$, $L\in\mathcal L_Y$, steps 4–5 give $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*L\in\mathcal L_X$ and $Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\in\mathcal L_Y$, so both sides of the projection map lie in $\mathcal L_Y$. Together with step 3, both sides are exact sum-preserving functors with either input fixed.

source.place: Paragraph (2), extension: preservation and direct sums of proper direct image and inverse image

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] to the proper $k$-morphism $p$ of standing schemes and $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and its section-ring sheaf. Its equivalences $D(E_X)$, $D(E_Y)$ are termwise extensions of exact additive equivalences, so they commute with shifts, cones and small sums; it identifies the module-object $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ with its unit and counit, and the K-flat tensors, with the ringed-topos ones, and it carries the module-object projection map of the statement to the ringed-topos map $\alpha_{K,L}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] itself. Use the canonical shift on $U=p^*$ and the adjunction-compatible shift on $R=Rp_*$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique](iii); [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] gives exactness of $R$ with this shift. In the $L$ variable the mate is a transformation of exact functors by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; in the $K$ variable it is one by [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift]. Transport these shift structures through the exact equivalences to our module-object categories. Therefore the actual canonical map is natural and shift compatible in each input, including the connecting square of each distinguished triangle. The structures restrict to the full triangulated localizing subcategories of step 6, since the equivalences preserve sums and triangles.

source.place: Paragraph (2), extension: the canonical projection transformation is shift compatible in both variables; Stacks Tag 0943 (section-projection-formula), Tag 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact)

proof.text: Fix $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. The functors $K\mapsto Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$ and $K\mapsto Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*L)$ from $\mathcal L_X$ to $\mathcal L_Y$ are exact and preserve sums by step 6, and their canonical transformation is a transformation of exact functors by step 7. It is invertible on $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by step 2. Apply [sk-lem-sf-determination] with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and the $\Dctf=\Dbc$ identifications of step 1. It follows that $\pi_{K,L}$ is invertible for every $K\in\mathcal L_X$ and this bounded constructible $L$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), extension: first application of determination, in K

proof.text: Fix any $K\in\mathcal L_X$. Both functors of $L$ from $\mathcal L_Y$ to $\mathcal L_Y$ are exact and sum preserving by step 6, with a shift-compatible natural transformation by step 7. Step 8 proves its invertibility for every $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Apply [sk-lem-sf-determination] with source and target scheme both $Y$, again using step 1. The map is invertible for all $L\in\mathcal L_Y$. This proves the rest of (2), and even locates the isomorphism in the full target subcategory $\mathcal L_Y$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), extension: second application of determination, in L
